clue.text: Humiliated, he finally departs after a party

indicators.note: the clue puts the closing letters after the party, so they come at the end

parts.note: taken as written
a bash is an informal party

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of the word he

parts.note: only its last letter is used
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A man slinks off in shame at the end of a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abashed is to be embarrassed and made to feel ashamed, a close synonym of humiliated.

clue.text: Kidnap sailor on canal

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
a duct is a canal or channel, as in the body

explanation.surface: A sailor is snatched while out on a canal.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct someone is to carry them off by force, a direct synonym of kidnap.

clue.text: A horse's value

parts.note: taken as written
a mount is a horse one rides

explanation.surface: A question of what a horse is worth.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount is a quantity or sum, the value of something in total.

clue.text: Husband wearing shoes? Pity — bad idea

indicators.note: the husband's letter is worn inside the rest, as if clothed by it
bad shoes and pity are spoiled, so their letters are reshuffled

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A husband in ill-fitting shoes is pitied, and his footwear was a poor choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypothesis is a proposed explanation or theory, an idea put forward to be tested.

clue.text: Tot and adult play

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits, a dram

explanation.surface: A small child and a grown-up are performing a play together.
explanation.walkthrough: Tot looks like a toddler next to the adult, but it is a shot of whisky; A is the film certificate for adult.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play for the stage, radio or screen.

clue.text: Policeman perhaps in charge interrupting volunteer

indicators.note: the in-charge letters break into the middle of the volunteering word

parts.note: to volunteer something is to offer it

explanation.surface: A policeman in charge cuts in when someone offers to help.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer is a policeman; perhaps signals the policeman is one example of an officer.

clue.text: Two dismissals? Perfect!

wordplay.note: a batsman given out is dismissed, so two dismissals is one out and another out

explanation.surface: A bowler takes two wickets and the crowd cheers perfection.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a dismissed batsman is out.
explanation.definitionFit: Out-and-out means complete or utter, as in an out-and-out triumph, so perfect in the sense of absolute.

clue.text: Teen oddly follows female a lot

indicators.note: the teen letters follow the female and a, so they come last

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: oddly takes the first and third letters of the word

parts.note: only its odd letters are used

explanation.surface: A teenager tags along behind a woman a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot' reads as 'often', but lot is the definition and a is a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot is one's destiny in life, a synonym of fate.

clue.text: Embracing cold fish outside university disheartened dad

indicators.note: the cold-fish letters go around the university and dad pieces

parts.note: ling is a long cod-like sea fish

indicators.note: a word losing its heart keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: only its first and last letters are used

explanation.surface: A cold fish of a man is shut out of the university, leaving his father dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: A cold fish is an unfriendly person, but here cold and fish are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuddling someone means holding them close in one's arms, the same as embracing them.

clue.text: Answer from salesman about first of sculptures on small base

indicators.note: the salesman is placed about, that is around, the sculptures letter

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: only its first letter is used
taken as written
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A salesman answers questions about a display of sculptures on a small plinth.
explanation.definitionFit: A response is a reply given to a question, a synonym of answer.

clue.text: Decline flipping dreadful diamonds

indicators.note: flipping turns the dreadful-diamonds string end to end

parts.note: poor means of bad quality, dreadful

explanation.surface: A card player curses a decline in a run of dreadful diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: Flipping reads as a mild British curse but signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop is to sag or sink downward, so decline in the sense of falling away.

clue.text: Putt aside, playing shows skills

indicators.note: playing about with the letters rearranges them

parts.note: the letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A golfer who sets aside putting still shows plenty of skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Aptitudes are natural abilities or talents, a near synonym of skills.

clue.text: Prisoners exercise with time restriction

parts.note: cons is slang for convicts, prisoners
to train is to exercise

explanation.surface: Inmates may exercise only within a set time limit.
explanation.definitionFit: A constraint is a limit or check on action, a synonym of restriction.

clue.text: Original sole grips to boot

indicators.note: the two words grip the answer between them, holding it inside

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: An original shoe sole has good grip, as well as a fine boot.
explanation.walkthrough: Sole and boot make a shoe picture, but to boot is the idiom meaning in addition.
explanation.definitionFit: To boot is an idiom meaning in addition or besides, which also means too.

clue.text: Naughty child revises unexpectedly? Admirable

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters land in a surprising order

parts.note: the fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A naughty child revises for a test and surprisingly earns admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impressive commands respect or admiration, a near synonym of admirable.

clue.text: Devon temples spoiled housing estates?

indicators.note: the temples have been spoiled, so their letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Old temples in the Devon countryside ruined by new housing estates.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is an English county in the south-west.
explanation.definitionFit: A housing estate is a planned group of homes built together, an example of new building developments.

clue.text: They apparently never forget when pal set off without wife

indicators.note: set off, the letters go off and are rearranged
without here means lacking, so the wife's letter is dropped

parts.note: the word itself loses its first letter
these letters join the fodder

explanation.surface: A man sets off with a friend while leaving his wife behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Set off looks like a departure, but off is the anagram signal and set is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying that an elephant never forgets credits these animals with a long memory, hence apparently.

clue.text: Destitution's tough on son now

parts.note: hard means tough or difficult
hip means fashionable, now in slang

explanation.surface: Poverty is proving tough on a son today.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardship is suffering from lack of money or comforts, so it covers destitution.

clue.text: Support almost cutting marks for students

indicators.note: the support letters cut into the marks, sitting inside them

parts.note: scars are marks left on the skin

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to hold is to support

explanation.surface: Students given marks that nearly cut off their support.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholars are learned people or students holding scholarships at a school or university.

clue.text: Catherine curt about removing new make-up

indicators.note: the remaining letters are knocked about into a new order
the new letter is taken away from the fodder before rearranging

parts.note: the letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Catherine is curt about having her new make-up taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: Make-up suggests cosmetics, but here it means the way something is built.
explanation.definitionFit: Architecture can mean the structure or design of a thing, its overall make-up.

clue.text: Father — man up and put on a hat

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: the word itself is turned around
taken as written

explanation.surface: A father is told to man up and put on a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panama is a lightweight straw hat originally from Ecuador.

clue.text: Respect daydreaming? Not I !

indicators.note: not I tells us to leave the letter I out of the word

parts.note: reverie is a state of daydreaming
the letter I named in the clue is the one removed

explanation.surface: Someone insists they are no daydreamer and deserve respect.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere someone is to hold them in deep respect or awe.

clue.text: Fund's last with low returns? Catastrophe

indicators.note: last takes the end letter of the word fund

parts.note: only the final letter of fund is used

indicators.note: returns means the lowing sound comes back reversed

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow

explanation.surface: An investment fund ends up with poor returns, a financial disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Low returns sounds like poor profits; here low is a cow's moo.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom is ruin or a terrible fate, a synonym of catastrophe.

clue.text: One doesn't like spending money a great deal feeding Charlie and Kate

indicators.note: the great deal is fed into the middle of Charlie and Kate

parts.note: taken as written
heaps is informal for a lot

explanation.surface: Someone who hates spending feeds Charlie and Kate a great deal anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapskate is a stingy person, someone who avoids parting with money.

clue.text: Passage this writer will read out

indicators.note: read out aloud, the phrase is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: this writer is the setter, I, so the phrase is I'll

explanation.surface: The author promises to read a passage aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: Passage looks like the extract to be read, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, a passage.

clue.text: Reminder about third of walnuts — this is what you're trying to crack

definitions.text: this is what you're trying to crack

indicators.note: the reminder goes about, around, the walnut letter

parts.note: a cue is a prompt or reminder

indicators.note: third of takes the third letter of the next word

parts.note: only its third letter is used

explanation.surface: A note about walnuts, which you are trying to crack open.
explanation.walkthrough: Walnuts and crack make a nutcracker picture; what the solver cracks is this very thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Solvers crack each crossword prompt, so the definition describes the thing being read right now.

clue.text: Principal with punishment for pupils — they're often seen in rags

parts.note: the head is the principal of a school
lines are sentences a pupil must copy out as punishment

explanation.surface: A head teacher punishes pupils, who turn up in tattered clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Rags are scruffy clothes but also slang for tabloid newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Headlines are the large-print titles of stories in newspapers, which are called rags.

clue.text: Picture that is enthralling mother? Good!

indicators.note: enthralling holds captive, so that is wraps around the mother and good letters

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
ma is an informal mother

explanation.surface: A painting that has captivated mother is judged good.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness of something.

clue.text: Have groups of constables succeeded?

parts.note: a posse is a body of men summoned by a sheriff or constable

explanation.surface: A question of whether the police squads have got their man.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to own or hold it, a synonym of have.

clue.text: We'll leave as the regular characters exit lift

indicators.note: every other letter exits, so alternate letters starting with the second remain

parts.note: the even letters of these words give the answer

explanation.surface: Regular cast members leave a show, which is meant to give it a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate is to raise up, a synonym of lift.
